definitions.explanation: Treating someone in a cold, dismissive, or unkind manner. Describes behavior toward others rather than personality in general.

examples.japanese: {邪険|じゃけん}に{扱|あつか}う。
{子供|こども}を{邪険|じゃけん}にしてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not treat children unkindly.

examples.japanese: せっかく{訪|たず}ねてきた{客|きゃく}を{邪険|じゃけん}に{追|お}い{返|かえ}すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't just coldly turn away a guest who went out of their way to visit.

notes:
USAGE:
{邪険|じゃけん} almost always appears in the pattern {邪険|じゃけん}に + verb, functioning adverbially. It describes cold or dismissive treatment of a person.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {邪険|じゃけん}に{扱|あつか}う (to treat harshly)
- {邪険|じゃけん}にする (to be unkind to)
- {邪険|じゃけん}に{追|お}い{払|はら}う (to coldly chase away)

NUANCE:
{邪険|じゃけん} focuses specifically on treatment of people, implying the speaker feels the harshness is unjustified or excessive. It is not used to describe objects or situations.
